subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Volume of Cubes and Cuboids
seo_title: P5 Volume of Cubes and Cuboids Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Volume of cubes and cuboids; measuring volume in cubic units, cm³/m³; finding the volume of liquid in a rectangular tank; relationship between ℓ (or ml) with cm³
meta_desc: Free P5 volume worksheets: count unit cubes, length × breadth × height, cm³ and m³, 1 ℓ = 1000 cm³ and water in tanks. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Volume = length × breadth × height, in cubic units such as cm³ and m³.
key_sub: A box 6 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm has a volume of 6 × 4 × 5 = 120 cm³, and 1 ℓ = 1000 cm³.
body_html:
Volume is the number of unit cubes

Volume is the amount of space a solid takes up. A 1-cm cube has a volume of 1 cubic centimetre (1 cm³). Count the cubes in one layer, then multiply by the number of layers. Remember the hidden cubes.

Volume = length × breadth × height

For a cuboid, multiply the three lengths. A cube has equal edges, so multiply the edge by itself three times. Write the answer in cubic units: cm³ for small objects, m³ for large spaces such as rooms.

Example 1

A cube has edges of 5 cm. Find its volume.

5 × 5 × 5 = 25 × 5 = 125.

Answer: 125 cm³

Litres and cubic centimetres

1 ℓ = 1000 cm³ and 1 ml = 1 cm³. To change cm³ to litres, divide by 1000.

VolumeSame as
1 ml1 cm³
250 ml250 cm³
1 ℓ1000 cm³
2 ℓ 450 ml2450 cm³
30 000 cm³30 ℓ

Water in a rectangular tank

The water in a tank is a cuboid too. Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank. The empty part above the water tells you how much more is needed to fill the tank.

Example 2

How many more litres of water are needed to fill this tank to the brim?

Empty part: 40 − 30 = 10 cm high. 50 × 40 × 10 = 20 000 cm³ = 20 ℓ.

Answer: 20 ℓ

Word problems: use a model

When a tank is a fraction full, draw the tank as equal units. Find 1 unit first.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting only the cubes you can seeCount layer by layer, including hidden cubes
Adding the edges: 6 + 4 + 5 = 15Multiply: 6 × 4 × 5 = 120 cm³
Writing cm² for a volumeArea is cm², volume is cm³
1 ℓ = 100 cm³1 ℓ = 1000 cm³, and 1 ml = 1 cm³
Using the height of the tank for the waterUse the depth of the water

faq.q: What is taught about volume in P5 maths?
faq.a: Primary 5 students find the volume of solids made of unit cubes, find the volume of cubes and cuboids in cm³ and m³, and use 1 ℓ = 1000 cm³ to find the volume of water in a rectangular tank.

faq.q: How do I explain volume to my child?
faq.a: Build a cuboid with small cubes and count them layer by layer. Then show that length × breadth × height gives the same number, for example 4 × 2 × 3 = 24 cm³.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with volume?
faq.a: Counting only the cubes that can be seen, or adding the length, breadth and height instead of multiplying them. Another is thinking that 1 ℓ = 100 cm³; it is 1000 cm³.

faq.q: Is volume in the MOE syllabus for Primary 5?
faq.a: Yes. Volume of cubes and cuboids, cm³ and m³, and water in rectangular tanks are part of Area and Volume in the MOE Primary 5 syllabus. In Primary 6 students go on to find a missing length from the volume.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes make up this cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 2 rows of 4 cubes = 8 cubes. There are 3 layers: 8 × 3 = 24. Count the hidden cubes too (only 18 cubes can be seen).

items.q: The cuboid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 2 layers: 9 × 2 = 18. Count the hidden cubes too (only 14 cubes can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 3 layers: 9 × 3 = 27. Count the hidden cubes too (only 19 cubes can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes are used to build this solid?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 3 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 12 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 9 can be seen).

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 10 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 9 can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes are used to build this solid?

items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 14 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 9 can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes are used to build this solid?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 22 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 16 can be seen).

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 24 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 16 can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many more 1-cm cubes are needed to make a cube with edges of 3 cm?
items.e: A cube with edges of 3 cm has 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cubes. The solid has 3 + 6 + 9 = 18 cubes. 27 − 18 = 9 more.

items.q: How many more 1-cm cubes are needed to make a cuboid 3 cm long, 2 cm wide and 3 cm high?
items.e: The cuboid needs 3 × 2 × 3 = 18 cubes. The solid has 3 + 7 = 10 cubes. 18 − 10 = 8 more.

items.q: How many more 1-cm cubes are needed to make a cube with edges of 3 cm?
items.e: A cube with edges of 3 cm has 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cubes. The solid has 7 cubes (one is hidden at the back). 27 − 7 = 20 more. (1 more cube would only make a cube with edges of 2 cm.)

items.q: Both solids are made of 1-cm cubes. How much greater is the volume of Solid A than Solid B?
items.e: Solid A: 3 × 2 × 3 = 18 cm³. Solid B: 3 + 5 + 6 = 14 cm³. 18 − 14 = 4 cm³. Count the hidden cubes in both.

items.q: Both solids are made of 1-cm cubes. What is their total volume?
items.e: Solid A: 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 cm³. Solid B: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 cm³. Total = 12 + 6 = 18 cm³.

items.q: A cuboid is made of 1-cm cubes. Each layer has 4 rows of 6 cubes. There are 3 layers. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer = 4 × 6 = 24 cubes. 3 layers = 24 × 3 = 72 cubes = 72 cm³.

items.q: Wei Ming fills a box with 1-cm cubes. The bottom layer has 15 cubes. The box holds 4 layers. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: 15 cubes in each layer × 4 layers = 60 cubes. The volume is 60 cm³.

items.q: Farah builds a cube with edges of 4 cm from 1-cm cubes. How many cubes does she use?
items.e: 4 × 4 = 16 cubes in each layer. There are 4 layers: 16 × 4 = 64 cubes.

items.q: Mei Ling's pencil box is 14 cm long. Its breadth is half its length, and its height is 4 cm. What is the volume of the pencil box?
items.e: Breadth = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm. Volume = 14 × 7 × 4 = 98 × 4 = 392 cm³.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the volume of a dice?
items.e: Volume uses cubic units. Use cm³ for small objects you can hold and m³ for large spaces such as rooms. cm² and m² are units of area.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the volume of a classroom?
items.e: Volume uses cubic units. Use cm³ for small objects you can hold and m³ for large spaces such as rooms. cm² and m² are units of area.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the volume of a box of tissues?
items.e: Volume uses cubic units. Use cm³ for small objects you can hold and m³ for large spaces such as rooms. cm² and m² are units of area.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the volume of the inside of a lorry?
items.e: Volume uses cubic units. Use cm³ for small objects you can hold and m³ for large spaces such as rooms. cm² and m² are units of area.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the volume of an eraser?
items.e: An eraser is about 4 cm by 2 cm by 1 cm, so about 8 cm³. 8 m³ would fill a cube 2 m wide, and cm² is for area.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the volume of a classroom?
items.e: A classroom is about 9 m by 8 m by 3 m: 9 × 8 × 3 = 216 m³. So about 200 m³.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the volume of a shoebox?
items.e: A shoebox is about 30 cm by 20 cm by 12 cm: 30 × 20 × 12 = 7200 cm³. So about 7000 cm³.

items.q: The diagram shows the shape of a storeroom. Find its volume.
items.e: Volume = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 m³. The lengths are in metres, so the volume is in cubic metres (m³).

items.q: The diagram shows the shape of a container. Find its volume.
items.e: Volume = 6 × 2 × 3 = 36 m³. The lengths are in metres, so the volume is in cubic metres (m³).

items.q: The diagram shows the shape of a school hall. Find its volume.
items.e: Volume = 20 × 15 × 6 = 1800 m³. The lengths are in metres, so the volume is in cubic metres (m³).

items.q: A storage box is 2.5 m long, 2 m wide and 1 m high. Find its volume.
A cube has edges of 3 m. Find its volume.
items.e: Volume = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 m³. 9 m² is the area of one face.

items.q: Which measurement is a volume?
items.e: Volume is measured in cubic units such as m³ and cm³. m² is an area, m is a length and kg is a mass.

items.q: Box A is 10 cm by 8 cm by 5 cm. Box B is 9 cm by 7 cm by 6 cm. Which box has the greater volume, and by how much?
Box A is 12 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. Box B is 8 cm by 8 cm by 5 cm. Which box has the greater volume, and by how much?
Box A is 15 cm by 4 cm by 4 cm. Box B is 10 cm by 6 cm by 3 cm. Which box has the greater volume, and by how much?
A solid is made of two cuboids. One cuboid is 6 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm. The other is 2 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm. What is the volume of the solid?
Ahmad stacks a box 30 cm by 20 cm by 10 cm on top of a box 40 cm by 30 cm by 20 cm. What is the total volume of the two boxes?
Which box has the greatest volume?
items.e: 6 × 6 × 6 = 216, 10 × 10 × 2 = 200, 12 × 4 × 4 = 192, 20 × 3 × 3 = 180 (all in cm³). The box with the longest edges is not always the biggest: multiply, do not add.

items.q: Which box has the smallest volume?
items.e: 10 × 2 × 1 = 20, 4 × 3 × 2 = 24, 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 (all in cm³). The longest box has the smallest volume: multiply, do not add.

items.e: 3080 cm³ = 3080 ml = 3000 ml + 80 ml = 3 ℓ 80 ml. The thousands are the litres.

items.e: 1605 cm³ = 1605 ml = 1000 ml + 605 ml = 1 ℓ 605 ml. The thousands are the litres.

items.q: The water in the tank is 20 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 40 × 30 × 20 = 24 000 cm³ = 24 ℓ.

items.q: The water in the tank is 35 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 60 × 40 × 35 = 84 000 cm³ = 84 ℓ.

items.q: The water in the tank is 28 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 50 × 25 × 28 = 35 000 cm³ = 35 ℓ.

items.q: How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 60 − 35 = 25 cm high. 50 × 40 × 25 = 50 000 cm³ = 50 ℓ.

items.q: How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 45 − 25 = 20 cm high. 40 × 30 × 20 = 24 000 cm³ = 24 ℓ.

items.q: How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 40 − 15 = 25 cm high. 60 × 30 × 25 = 45 000 cm³ = 45 ℓ.

items.q: A tank 40 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high contains 32 ℓ of water. How many more litres of water are needed to fill it completely?
items.e: Capacity = 40 × 40 × 50 = 80 000 cm³ = 80 ℓ. More water needed = 80 − 32 = 48 ℓ.

items.q: A tank is 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. It contains 27 ℓ 500 ml of water. How much more water is needed to fill it?
A tank is 60 cm long, 50 cm wide and 40 cm high. It is 34 full of water. How many litres of water are in it?
items.e: Capacity = 60 × 50 × 40 = 120 000 cm³ = 120 ℓ. 34 of 120 ℓ = 120 ÷ 4 × 3 = 90 ℓ.

items.q: A tank is 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. It is 23 full of water. How many litres of water are in it?
items.e: Capacity = 50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 cm³ = 60 ℓ. 23 of 60 ℓ = 60 ÷ 3 × 2 = 40 ℓ.

items.q: Mrs Lim's fish tank is 25 full. It has 24 ℓ of water in it. How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank?
items.e: 2 units = 24 ℓ, so 1 unit = 12 ℓ. The empty part is 3 units = 3 × 12 = 36 ℓ. (The full tank is 5 units = 60 ℓ.)

items.q: A tank is 14 full of water. After 30 ℓ of water is added, it is 34 full. What is the capacity of the tank?
items.e: The 30 ℓ fills 34 − 14 = 24 of the tank. 2 units = 30 ℓ, so 1 unit = 15 ℓ. Capacity = 4 units = 4 × 15 = 60 ℓ.

items.q: Tank A has 3 times as much water as Tank B. Together they hold 48 ℓ of water. How much water is in Tank A?
items.e: 4 units = 48 ℓ, so 1 unit = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 ℓ. Tank A = 3 units = 3 × 12 = 36 ℓ. (16 ℓ is 48 ÷ 3.)

items.q: Tank P has 15 ℓ more water than Tank Q. Together they hold 75 ℓ of water. How much water is in Tank Q?
items.e: Take away the extra 15 ℓ: 75 − 15 = 60 ℓ. This is 2 equal parts, so Tank Q = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 ℓ. Tank P = 30 + 15 = 45 ℓ.

items.q: An empty tank is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high. A tap fills it at 8 ℓ per minute. How long does it take to fill the tank?
A tank 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 45 cm high has water 15 cm deep. Water flows in from a tap at 6 ℓ per minute. How long will it take to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 45 − 15 = 30 cm high: 50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 cm³ = 60 ℓ. Time = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 min. (15 min would fill the whole tank of 90 ℓ.)

items.q: A tank 40 cm long, 30 cm wide and 25 cm high is full of water. Devi pours all the water into bottles. Each bottle holds 750 ml. How many bottles can she fill?
The school's water tank is 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 60 cm high. It is 40% full. How many litres of water are in it?
Ali's fish tank is 24 cm long, 15 cm wide and 20 cm high. The water in it is 13 cm deep. What is the volume of the water in litres and millilitres?
items.e: Water = 24 × 15 × 13 = 360 × 13 = 4680 cm³ = 4680 ml = 4 ℓ 680 ml. Use the depth (13 cm), not the height.

items.q: Mr Tan's tank is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. It is full of water. He fills 3 pails with water from the tank. Each pail holds 8 ℓ 500 ml. How much water is left in the tank?
items.e: Capacity = 60 × 40 × 30 = 72 000 cm³ = 72 ℓ. Water used = 3 × 8 ℓ 500 ml = 25 ℓ 500 ml. 72 ℓ − 25 ℓ 500 ml = 46 ℓ 500 ml.
